name: mint-iter-nethermind-probe
description: ItWorksinMyLocal#62 / xdc-nethermind-private#250 nethermind S1/S2-follow probe: same 3-oldxdc-sealer trusted quorum as mint-iter.json, but instead of a role=proposer candidate (topo.sh hard-rejects role=proposer for client nethermind -- no sealing-flag path wired, and upstream InitBlockProducer is a hard NotSupportedException, xdc-nethermind-private#224), nethermind is joined here as a plain role=follower node ('nm1') to answer one narrow question honestly: with #250's genesis->chainspec converter (netlab/nm-chainspec.sh, auto-invoked by join.sh) now lifting the old chainId==5151-only rejection, can nethermind at least reach S1 (syncs)/S2 (follows-at-tip, clean) against a live oldxdc XDPoS quorum on a custom, per-run chainId -- or does it hit the converter's own known live wall (a genesis-block state-root divergence from nethermind's TIPSigning-at-genesis default, documented in nm-chainspec.sh's header and #250). Same chain shape as mint-iter.json (period=1, epoch=900, reward=5000, gap=450) so results are directly comparable; v2block fixed at 1800 (V1-focus) since S1/S2 is the question, not the V1->V2 switch. Separate portBase (34305) from every other topology file's own range so this can run standalone or alongside them.
